title: Running Muse Code Models Inside Claude Code: A Setup Guide

facts.fact: Meta shipped its Muse Code terminal coding agent in beta on August 5, 2026.
facts.quote: Meta shipped its own terminal coding agent, _**[Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/)**_, in beta on August 5, 2026

facts.fact: The Muse Spark model family is currently on version 1.3.
facts.quote: The model family is **Muse Spark**, currently on version 1.3, and it ships in two pricing tiers

facts.fact: The blog author reports that the Muse Spark Contributor tier is roughly 12x cheaper than Standard on input tokens and roughly 21x cheaper on output tokens.
facts.quote: That’s roughly a **12x** discount on input and a **21x** discount on output.

facts.fact: The blog author states Contributor is a roughly 20x cost cut relative to Standard pricing.
facts.quote: a ~20x cost cut is hard to argue with

facts.fact: Pricing for Muse Spark is a straight pass-through of token costs with no separate license fee.
facts.quote: Pricing is a straight pass-through of token costs, no separate license fee:

facts.fact: Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor has a native context window of about 1,048,576 tokens (1M), according to the blog.
facts.quote: Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor actually has a native ~1,048,576-token (1M) context window, larger than Claude’s default 200K assumption.

facts.fact: Claude Code's default context assumption is 200K tokens.
When Claude Code receives an unrecognized model ID, it silently defaults the auto-compact window to 1 token.
facts.quote: it silently defaults the **auto-compact window to 1 token**

facts.fact: The Standard tier does not use prompts or completions for training, according to Meta's claim as reported by the blog.
facts.quote: Meta does not use your prompts or completions for training, so they claim.

facts.fact: The Contributor tier lets Meta use prompts and completions to improve its products in exchange for a steep discount.
facts.quote: a steep discount in exchange for letting Meta use your prompts and completions to improve its products.

facts.fact: The two Muse Spark tiers are selected by model ID: muse-spark-1.3 for Standard and muse-spark-1.3-contributor for Contributor.
Contributor tier is rate-limited well below Standard, so heavy concurrent sessions may be throttled on Contributor sooner.
facts.quote: Contributor is rate-limited well below Standard, so a team running heavy concurrent agent sessions may hit throttling on Contributor

facts.fact: Most third-party comparisons, per the blog, place Muse Code below Claude Code but ahead of Codex CLI on raw benchmark quality.
facts.quote: most third-party comparisons place Muse Code below Claude Code but ahead of Codex CLI.

facts.fact: The MODEL_API_KEY used for the Claude Code endpoint comes from a Meta Model API account, separate from the muse CLI OAuth login.
facts.quote: Get `MODEL_API_KEY` from your Meta Model API account, not from the `muse` CLI’s own OAuth login

facts.fact: Using the [1m] suffix on a custom model ID is described as an unsupported workaround documented only for known Anthropic model names.
facts.quote: Officially, this suffix is documented only for known Anthropic model names, using it against a custom model ID is a workaround, not a supported path

facts.fact: The page advises removing "-contributor" from every model ID listed above when working with anything the user would not want Meta to train on.
facts.quote: Swap_`-contributor`_out of every model ID above if you’re working with anything you wouldn’t want Meta training on; the pricing difference is real, but so is what you’re trading for it.
